name: ENS–PSL International Selection (Sélection internationale)
application_deadline: 16 October – 15 December 2026, 14:00 Paris time, on OnePSL30 (Arts & Humanities and Sciences)
call_notes: 2027 selection open now (checked 30 October 2026). Applicants must not have turned 26 by 16 October 2026, and anyone who has applied in an earlier year cannot apply again.
benefits: A room on an ENS campus. Selected students follow the ENS diploma over three years, usually alongside a master's.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
2027 selection (open now):
Applications: 16 October 2026, 14:00 – 15 December 2026, 14:00 (Paris time), both tracks.

Arts & Humanities: shortlist from 21 January 2027; tests 15–26 February 2027; results from 9 March 2027.
Sciences: shortlist from 27 January 2027; tests 3–19 March 2027; results from 26 March 2027.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Not yet 26 on 16 October 2026, the opening date.
Studying at a foreign university:
Arts & Humanities: at least 3 years of study towards a foreign university degree.
Sciences: at least 1 year of foreign undergraduate study when applying, and 2 by enrolment.
Limited time in France:
Arts & Humanities: no more than 10 months living in France during the year of the competition or the year before.
Sciences: no more than 6 months in total enrolled at a French school or university during those years.
One attempt only: anyone who applied in an earlier year cannot apply again.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
€1,000 a month for 36 months.
A room on an ENS campus.
Selected students study for the ENS diploma, usually alongside a master's at ENS or a PSL partner. NOTE — verify with ENS which registration fees remain for the national degree.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Check the age and study conditions for the track (Arts & Humanities or Sciences).
2. Apply on OnePSL30 (concoursens.candidature.onepsl30.fr) between 16 October and 15 December 2026, 14:00 Paris time.
3. Upload the documents and arrange 2–4 recommendation letters.

5. Results from 9 March (Arts & Humanities) or 26 March 2027 (Sciences).
6. If selected: Études en France, then the visa.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
CV.
Motivation letter, 1–3 pages.
Research project, 3 pages at most.
University transcripts.
School-leaving diploma (HSSC / A-levels).
2 to 4 recommendation letters.
Passport.
NOTE — verify the language of the tests for the chosen track on ENS's FAQ before the student applies.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Études en France (EeF) through Campus France Pakistan comes before the visa: an online file, then an academic interview at Alliance Française in Karachi, Lahore or Islamabad, with original documents.
Attestation Campus France Pakistan asks for: SSC/O-level and HSSC/A-level documents attested by IBCC; bachelor's degree and transcript attested by HEC; passport valid until 18 months after the visa appointment; IELTS or other English proof; CV with experience letters; gap letter if any; the final acceptance letter.

For the visa the student must show resources for the year, about €615 a month (NOTE — verify the current figure). Where the scholarship pays no living allowance, this has to come from family funds or a sponsor.

This is for strong students part-way through a bachelor's (Sciences) or near its end (Arts & Humanities), not for older graduates: check the 26-year limit and the years-of-study rule first.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Applying at 26 or older on 16 October 2026.
Applying to Arts & Humanities with fewer than 3 years of university study.
Applying a second time after an earlier attempt.

name: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt Programme (Public Policy and Good Governance)
region: National — German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD), funded by the Federal Foreign Office
application_deadline: Closed for 2027/2028 (window was 1 June – 31 July 2026; results December 2026 / January 2027). Next window expected June – July 2027 for courses starting in autumn 2028.
call_notes: Checked 30 October 2026 against DAAD's 2026 call and FAQ (both dated 05/2026). Pakistan is on the country list. Students apply to the courses, not to DAAD.
stipend_amount: €992 a month, + a study and research grant of €460 a year
benefits: No tuition fees; health, accident and personal liability insurance; travel allowance; rent subsidy and family allowances where they apply; a German course of up to 4 months in Germany before the master's.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
2027/2028 intake: closed. Applications ran 1 June – 31 July 2026. Selection committees meet October/November 2026; results December 2026 / January 2027. Courses start September/October 2027.

Next round: expected 1 June – 31 July 2027, for courses starting in autumn 2028. NOTE — verify when DAAD publishes the 2027 call (usually May).

Students who want an autumn 2028 start should prepare now: work experience, grades, IELTS and motivation letter.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Graduates from countries on DAAD's list. Pakistan is on it.
A bachelor's degree in social or political science, law, economics, public policy or a related field, with grades in the upper third of the class.
Degree issued no earlier than 1 January 2020 (for the 2027 intake; expect the cut-off to move a year for 2028).
Practical experience is an essential requirement: work, internships, volunteering, or NGO or political work. DAAD sets no minimum; each course does, in DAAD's "Information about the Master's Courses" PDF.
Not more than 15 months spent in a non-DAC country by the application deadline (31 July).
A social and political commitment that fits public policy and good governance.

sections.title: The seven courses
sections.body:
Hochschule Bonn-Rhein-Sieg: Social Protection
University of Duisburg-Essen: Development and Governance
University of Erfurt: Public Policy
Otto von Guericke University Magdeburg: Peace and Conflict Studies
Osnabrück University of Applied Sciences: Management in Nonprofit Organisations
University of Passau: Development Studies
University of Passau: Governance and Public Policy

A student may apply to at most two of them, with the same motivation letter.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
€992 a month (DAAD master's rate).
A study and research grant of €460 a year.
No tuition fees.
Health, accident and personal liability insurance.
A lump-sum travel allowance.
Rent subsidy and family allowances where they apply.
A compulsory German course in Germany of up to 4 months before the master's, also funded.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Read DAAD's call and FAQ, then the "Information about the Master's Courses" PDF for each course's own requirements.
2. Pick at most two courses.
3. Apply directly to the courses, by their own procedure, within the window (last year 1 June – 31 July). Do not send anything to DAAD at this stage.
4. Courses shortlist and pass their nominees to DAAD; the selection committee meets in October/November.
5. Nominees are invited to complete the DAAD portal application.
6. Results in December/January; German course from spring/summer; master's from September/October.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
DAAD application form and checklist (from the call).
Europass CV.
Motivation letter, the same for both courses.
Degree certificate and transcripts, certified (HEC-attested for Pakistani degrees).
Proof of practical experience (employer or organisation letters).
English proof (IELTS or TOEFL at the level each course sets).
Recommendation letter(s) as the courses ask.
NOTE — verify each course's list; they differ.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Blocked account for the visa: €11,904 for the year (€992 a month), the rate in force since 1 January 2025 and unchanged as of October 2026. A scholarship that pays at least that much replaces it, with the award letter.
APS is not required of Pakistani students.
Degrees and transcripts: HEC attestation for university documents, IBCC for school documents.
Visa appointments at the German Embassy Islamabad or Consulate Karachi are scarce: book as soon as the admission letter arrives.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Applying to DAAD instead of to the courses.
Applying to more than two courses, or writing a different motivation letter for each.
Graduating before 1 January 2020 (or the 2028 equivalent).
No practical experience at all, or none that fits the course.
Waiting for the window to open in June to start the IELTS and documents.

name: Deutschlandstipendium
region: National — federal government with private sponsors, awarded by each university
application_deadline: Set by each university, usually once a year in spring or summer for the following winter semester. New students can apply if they meet the university's entry requirements.
call_notes: A standing national programme; each university runs its own call. Checked 30 October 2026 on deutschlandstipendium.de. Open to all nationalities, so Pakistani students enrolled or admitted in Germany can apply.
stipend_amount: €300 a month (€150 from a private sponsor + €150 from the federal government)
benefits: Paid for at least two semesters, up to the end of the standard period of study. Income-independent; can be held with BAföG with no deduction. Many universities add mentoring and events with the sponsor.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
There is no national deadline. Each participating university sets its own window, usually once a year in spring or summer for awards starting in the winter semester.
Check the target university's "Deutschlandstipendium" page as soon as the student is admitted. NOTE — verify the university's own dates.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Students of any nationality, international students included.
Enrolled at a participating German university, or about to start there and meeting its entry requirements.
Selected on grades and achievement, and also on social commitment and personal circumstances (for example a migration background, family responsibilities, or working alongside study).
It cannot be held alongside talent-based support averaging €30 a month or more. A full DAAD scholarship rules it out; a partial one does not.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
€300 a month: €150 from a private sponsor (a company, foundation or individual) and €150 from the federal government.
Awarded for at least two semesters, and at most up to the end of the standard period of study.
Not means-tested and not counted against BAföG.
It is a top-up, not full funding: it does not replace the blocked account for the visa.

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Get admitted to (or enrol at) a participating university.
2. Find the university's Deutschlandstipendium page and its application window.
3. Apply through the university's own online form in that window.
4. The university's selection committee decides; some interview.
5. Awards usually start with the winter semester.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
The university's online form.
CV.
Transcripts (school results for new students; university results for current students).
Motivation letter.
Evidence of social commitment, work, or family circumstances, if relevant.
Recommendation letter, if the university asks.
NOTE — verify the university's own list.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Blocked account for the visa: €11,904 for the year (€992 a month), the rate in force since 1 January 2025 and unchanged as of October 2026. A scholarship that pays at least that much replaces it, with the award letter.
APS is not required of Pakistani students.
Degrees and transcripts: HEC attestation for university documents, IBCC for school documents.
Visa appointments at the German Embassy Islamabad or Consulate Karachi are scarce: book as soon as the admission letter arrives.

Deutschlandstipendium does not help with the visa: it is applied for after admission and pays €300 a month, well short of the blocked-account amount. Present it as a second-semester top-up, not as funding to get to Germany.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Treating it as funding that covers living costs or the blocked account.
Waiting for a national call. Each university runs its own.
Holding a full DAAD scholarship at the same time.
Missing the university's window because it falls before arrival.

name: German Political Foundations' Scholarships (Böll, KAS, FES, HSS, FNF)
region: National — party-affiliated foundations funded by the federal government
application_deadline: Each foundation has its own: Hanns Seidel 15 Nov 2026 – 31 Jan 2027 (12:00 CET), then 15 May – 15 Jul 2027 · Heinrich Böll 15 Jan – 1 Mar 2027 · Friedrich Ebert by 30 Nov (winter semester) or 31 May (summer semester) of the first semester · Konrad Adenauer 15 July 2027, 12:00 CET for applicants in Germany, otherwise via KAS offices abroad.
call_notes: Checked 30 October 2026 on each foundation's site. Every one needs good German (B2), and most fund only students already at or admitted to a German university. A route for German-speaking students, not for a student starting from Pakistan in English.
stipend_amount: KAS and FES: €992 a month for students; KAS PhD €1,400. Böll and Hanns Seidel amounts: NOTE — verify.
benefits: Health insurance allowance (KAS up to €120), family allowances (KAS €276 for a spouse, €250 per child; FES €255 per child), and seminars and networks run by the foundation.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
Hanns Seidel Foundation (HSS), international students and doctoral candidates: 15 November 2026 – 31 January 2027, 12:00 CET; then 15 May – 15 July 2027, 12:00 CEST.
Heinrich Böll Foundation: 15 January – 1 March 2027. The 15 July – 1 September 2026 round has closed. NOTE — verify: Böll's page mentions a change from 1 March 2027.
Friedrich Ebert Foundation (FES): before or at the start of the first semester — by 30 November for the winter semester, by 31 May for the summer semester.
Konrad Adenauer Foundation (KAS): 15 July 2027, 12:00 CET for applicants already in Germany; applicants abroad go through the KAS office in their country.
Friedrich Naumann Foundation (FNF): see its page for the current deadlines.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
All of them want strong grades and evident commitment to society, in line with the foundation's political values (Green, Christian Democrat, Social Democrat, Christian Social, Liberal). Interviews are part of selection.

Heinrich Böll (Green): priority for applicants from developing (DAC) countries not yet living in Germany; master's and PhD; only master's programmes of 4 semesters or more. German at B2 or above. NOTE — verify the language rule.
Konrad Adenauer (CDU): more than 50 countries; bachelor's from the 2nd semester, master's (4-semester programmes) or PhD; no age limit; German B2 by the start of studies. NOTE — verify Pakistan is among KAS's countries with the KAS office in Islamabad (info.pakistan@kas.de).
Friedrich Ebert (SPD): must already be studying at a German state or state-recognised university; German at B2.
Hanns Seidel (CSU): international students and doctoral candidates with German at B2. NOTE — verify the age limit and other conditions in HSS's guidelines.
Friedrich Naumann (FDP): non-EU students for a full-time master's or PhD in Germany (no bachelor's). Application and interview in German; applicants still abroad may be interviewed by video.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
Konrad Adenauer: up to €992 a month (PhD €1,400), up to €120 for health insurance, €276 for a spouse, €250 per child.
Friedrich Ebert: €992 a month plus health insurance; €255 per child. NOTE — verify the postgraduate rate (reported as €1,500).
Heinrich Böll: NOTE — verify the current monthly rate on Böll's site.
Hanns Seidel: NOTE — verify the current monthly rate in HSS's guidelines.
All add seminars, mentoring and an alumni network. None pays tuition (public universities in Germany charge none, apart from Baden-Württemberg's non-EU fee).

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Make sure the student's German is at B2 (certificate: Goethe, telc, TestDaF or DSH) and that they hold, or are about to hold, a place at a German university.
2. Pick the one foundation whose values the student genuinely shares; the interview tests this.
3. Apply on the foundation's online portal in its window (KAS: campus.kas.de; HSS: stipendienbewerbung.hss.de).
4. Shortlisted applicants are interviewed, often in two stages, in German.
5. Awards start with the next semester.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
Online form.
CV in table form (German style).
Motivation letter in German, explaining the student's social or political commitment.
Degree certificates and transcripts (HEC-attested), with German translations where asked.
University admission letter or enrolment certificate.
German certificate (B2).
One or two academic references; some foundations also want a reference on the student's commitment.
NOTE — verify each foundation's own list.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
Blocked account for the visa: €11,904 for the year (€992 a month), the rate in force since 1 January 2025 and unchanged as of October 2026. A scholarship that pays at least that much replaces it, with the award letter.
APS is not required of Pakistani students.
Degrees and transcripts: HEC attestation for university documents, IBCC for school documents.
Visa appointments at the German Embassy Islamabad or Consulate Karachi are scarce: book as soon as the admission letter arrives.

These awards suit a Pakistani student who already speaks German, or who is in Germany and has learned it. A student planning an English-taught master's from Pakistan should look at DAAD EPOS or Helmut-Schmidt instead.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Applying without German. Every foundation here requires B2.
Applying to a foundation whose politics the student cannot speak to in the interview.
Applying to several foundations at once. They are expected to be alternatives; one award at a time.
Assuming Böll funds one-year or 3-semester masters. It funds only 4-semester ones.

name: Scholarship Programme for Christian Young People (SCYP — Hungary Helps)
region: National — Hungary Helps (State Secretariat for the Aid of Persecuted Christians)
application_deadline: SUSPENDED — no new students were admitted for 2026/2027, and no 2027/2028 call has been published (checked 30 October 2026).
call_notes: On 6 August 2026 the SCYP portal announced that, by decision of Hungary's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, no new students would be admitted for 2026/2027. Do not promise this scholarship to a student until a new call appears on apply.scyp.hu.
stipend_amount: Suspended. Last published rates (2026/2027 call): HUF 166,600 a month for bachelor's and master's; PhD HUF 140,000, then 180,000.
benefits: Last published (2026/2027): tuition-free study, a dormitory place or HUF 40,000 a month for housing, HUF 200,000 a year towards travel, insurance up to HUF 65,000 a year. Not current while the programme is suspended.

sections.title: Status: suspended
sections.body:
On 6 August 2026 the SCYP portal said: "due to the decision of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, no new students will be admitted to the Scholarship Programme for Christian Young People for the 2026/2027 academic year".
No 2027/2028 call, deadline, country list or rates have been published as of 30 October 2026.
Students already on SCYP continue; this concerns new applicants.
Check apply.scyp.hu/news/archive before advising anyone. If a 2027/2028 call appears, update this guide from the new call PDF.

sections.title: How it worked (2026/2027 call, for reference)
sections.body:
Who: Christian young people from listed countries where Christians face persecution or discrimination (Pakistan was explicitly eligible for 2026/2027), who are members of a listed denomination and hold a recommendation from their church, approved by the State Secretariat.
Levels: bachelor's, one-tier and master's; PhD only for SCYP master's graduates.
Age: at least 18 by 31 August of the intake year.
Timeline: call October–November; deadline 10 January 23:59 CET; church approval by 15 February; admission decisions by 30 April; final decision by 15 June; arrival 1 September.
Pay: HUF 166,600 a month (bachelor's and master's); PhD HUF 140,000, then 180,000; dormitory or HUF 40,000 a month; HUF 200,000 a year for travel; insurance up to HUF 65,000 a year.
Application: online on apply.scyp.hu, with a typed English recommendation letter from the church giving the applicant's details.

sections.title: What to tell a student now
sections.body:
Do not build a plan on SCYP for 2027/2028 until a new call is published.
Christian students from Pakistan can apply to Stipendium Hungaricum instead, through HEC (see that guide); its 2027/2028 call is expected in November 2026.
Keep the church recommendation in hand, in case SCYP reopens with a short window.

name: Swedish University Tuition-Fee Scholarships
region: Swedish universities' own scholarships for non-EU fee payers
application_deadline: Master's application on universityadmissions.se by 15 January 2027 (fee and documents by 1 February), with the programme as priority 1. Then each university's own window: KTH 1 Dec 2026–15 Jan 2027; Chalmers late Nov 2026–mid Jan 2027; Uppsala 16 Jan–1 Feb 2027; Karolinska 8–24 Feb 2027; Lund early Feb 2027; Gothenburg by invitation ~10 Feb 2027; Umeå 5 Mar 2027; Linköping early Apr 2027; Stockholm by email after admission results.
call_notes: Pakistan is not eligible for the Swedish Institute's SISGP, so the universities' own tuition scholarships are the realistic route. Dates checked on each university's page on 30 October 2026. Most cover tuition only, and a tuition-only award does not count towards Migrationsverket's living-cost requirement.
stipend_amount: Tuition reduction or waiver: full tuition at KTH, Uppsala, Stockholm and Gothenburg; part or all at Lund, Karolinska and Umeå; usually 50% at Linköping; partial at Chalmers. Living costs are not paid.
benefits: Tuition only. Travel, insurance and living costs are the student's, and the residence permit still needs proof of SEK 10,656 a month (2026 rate) for the whole permit period.

sections.title: Important dates
sections.body:
University Admissions (universityadmissions.se), international round for programmes starting autumn 2027:
Opens: 16 October 2026
Application deadline: 15 January 2027
Application fee and supporting documents by: 1 February 2027
Admission results: early April 2027

Each university's scholarship window (2027 intake):
KTH Scholarship: 1 December 2026 – 15 January 2027. Results 1 April 2027.
Chalmers: late November 2026 – mid-January 2027 (exact dates on Chalmers' page).
Uppsala University Global Scholarship: 16 January – 1 February 2027.
Karolinska Institutet Global Master's Scholarship: 8–24 February 2027. Results 26 April 2027; accept by 30 April 2027.
Lund University Global Scholarship (LUGS): opens early February 2027 (last round closed 16 February 2026). NOTE — verify the 2027 dates once Lund publishes them.
University of Gothenburg, Axel Adler Scholarship: invitation to apply sent around 10 February 2027. Master's results 12 April 2027.
Umeå University: register interest by 5 March, 23:59 CET, on the form sent by email invitation. Results late April. NOTE — verify: Umeå's page still quotes 2026 dates in places.
Linköping University: opens early April 2027; exact dates not yet published.
Stockholm University Scholarship Scheme: the form is emailed after the admission results, to the address used on University Admissions. Recipients are told by the end of April.

sections.title: Who can apply
sections.body:
Students who pay tuition in Sweden: citizens of countries outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland. Pakistani students qualify.
Applying for a master's programme starting in autumn 2027 through University Admissions, in the international round (deadline 15 January 2027).
Almost every scheme requires the programme to be ranked priority 1 on University Admissions and the student to be admitted in that first round. Stockholm, Uppsala, KTH, Lund, Karolinska, Gothenburg and Linköping all say so.
Selection is on academic merit and motivation. Linköping asks for a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 or equivalent.

Competition is intense:
KTH nominated 65 of 718 applicants in 2026 (9%).
Karolinska gave 12 awards from 1,002 applicants in 2026.
Uppsala says about 2% of applicants receive its Global Scholarship.
Gothenburg gives one Axel Adler award per master's programme, plus up to ten more.

sections.title: What it pays
sections.body:
KTH Scholarship: full tuition for years 1 and 2. Year 2 depends on satisfactory first-year results.
Uppsala University Global Scholarship: full tuition.
Stockholm University Scholarship Scheme: the whole tuition fee.
Karolinska Institutet Global Master's Scholarship: tuition fees. NOTE — verify whether this is always the full fee; KI's page does not say.
Lund University Global Scholarship (LUGS): part or all of the tuition fee.
University of Gothenburg, Axel Adler Scholarship: the tuition fee.
Umeå University: a full or partial fee waiver.
Linköping University: tuition normally reduced by 50%.
Chalmers (Avancez, IPOET, US Friends of Chalmers, Adlerbert): partial tuition reductions. Chalmers' older pages give 75% for IPOET and Avancez (Avancez up to 85% in year 2 for strong results). NOTE — verify the 2027 percentages; the updated page does not yet give them.

None of these pays living costs, travel or insurance.
A tuition-only award does not count towards the residence-permit maintenance requirement (see For Pakistani students).

sections.title: How to apply
sections.body:
1. Shortlist master's programmes and read each university's scholarship page. Note which require priority 1 and any GPA threshold.
2. Apply on universityadmissions.se between 16 October 2026 and 15 January 2027. Put the programme at the university whose scholarship the student wants as priority 1. Only one programme can be first.
3. Pay the application fee and upload supporting documents by 1 February 2027.
4. Apply for the scholarship in that university's own window. KTH and Chalmers close by mid-January, with the admission deadline. Uppsala, Karolinska, Lund, Gothenburg, Umeå, Linköping and Stockholm come later, some by email invitation only, so watch the inbox used on University Admissions.
5. Admission results come in early April 2027 and scholarship results in April.
6. Accept the place and the scholarship, then apply for the residence permit on migrationsverket.se.

sections.title: Documents to prepare
sections.body:
For University Admissions:
Passport.
Bachelor's degree certificate and full transcripts, as University Admissions asks for Pakistani documents. NOTE — verify the Pakistan-specific rules on universityadmissions.se before uploading.
English proof (IELTS Academic, TOEFL, or another accepted route).
Programme-specific documents: CV, letter of intent, portfolio or course descriptions, as each programme asks.

For the scholarships:
Usually an online form and a motivation letter. Uppsala: a letter of at most 350 words and nothing uploaded. Lund: a letter of at most 600 words. Others vary.
Gothenburg, Umeå and Stockholm send their form by email after the admission stage.
NOTE — verify each university's list; they differ.

sections.title: For Pakistani students
sections.body:
The Swedish Institute's SISGP is not open to Pakistan (see the SISGP guide). These university scholarships are the route.

Residence permit (migrationsverket.se), after accepting the place:
Proof of SEK 10,656 a month for the whole permit period (rate for 2026 applications; the 2027 rate is not yet published). For 12 months that is about SEK 128,000.
A tuition scholarship does not count. A scholarship letter used as proof of funds must state that the student is the recipient, the period it covers, that it is for studies in Sweden, the amount, when it is paid, and how much is for living expenses.

New rules for permits granted from 11 June 2026:
Work capped at 15 hours a week during term. Work in June, July and August, and work at the university or linked to the programme, is not capped.
Study progress: at least 37.5 credits in year 1 and 45 credits a year from year 2. Falling short can lead to the permit being revoked or not extended.
The address must be registered within 30 days.

Budget plainly: even with a full tuition scholarship the family must show the living-cost money.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.body:
Not ranking the scholarship programme as priority 1 on University Admissions. Most schemes then rule the student out automatically.
Missing KTH and Chalmers, whose windows close in January with the admission deadline.
Waiting for an email from Gothenburg, Umeå or Stockholm at an address nobody checks.
Counting a tuition scholarship as proof of funds for the residence permit.
Applying for SISGP. Pakistan is not eligible.
Planning to cover living costs with part-time work. Term-time work is capped at 15 hours a week since June 2026.
Quoting Chalmers' old 75% figures without checking the 2027 page.
